purpose: Name every claim a native node is allowed to make, and say what each claim rests on, so a guarantee cannot cite a model that does not exist or a measurement nobody took.
note: `Guarantee::Native` carries a `semantic_model` string and the validator asked only that it not be empty. The frontend now builds the string from a closed vocabulary, and this file records the same vocabulary along with the recording behind each entry. A model with evidence is one whose behaviour was measured across the shells and whose measurement a gate re-runs. A model without evidence is one whose meaning is the IR operation's own definition - a sequence runs its statements in order - where there is nothing to measure; that is a different claim from having measured nothing, which is why the field is present and null rather than absent. The interpreter's name is prefixed at use, so an entry here is a suffix. `static-exit-checked-v1` reads its status at run time. For a decimal integer every shell agrees -- the value reduced modulo 256 -- and outside that they do not, so the model carries what the interpreter the plan names does: 255 for bash and /bin/sh, 0 for zsh, measured. A caller reading the status sees what it would have seen. What cannot be reproduced is the message bash writes, which names the interpreter's own path and a line number; the generated program names the value instead. The answer is carried in the IR as `NonNumericStatus`, so it is a value a reader and a gate can see rather than a note.
